sources.title: Arrangements for porting phone numbers when customers switch supplier
facts: The statement addressed rules for routing and porting fixed and mobile numbers.
An October 2008 update records that certain modifications were set aside following an appeal judgment.
limits: The record is historical and later regulatory versions govern current duties.

sources.title: Designing the broadband universal service obligation - Final report to Government
facts: Ofcom provided technical advice on options for a broadband universal service obligation.
The advice followed a call for inputs with 115 stakeholder responses.
limits: The page is historic policy-development evidence.
Cost estimates were preliminary and PDF internals were not used.

sources.title: Universal service obligations (broadband and telephony)
facts: BT and KCOM are designated universal service providers for broadband and telephony.
The broadband USO gives eligible homes and businesses a right to request a decent and affordable connection.
limits: A right to request is not a completed connection.
Designation does not prove current parcel orderability.

sources.title: Call for expressions of interest: Implementing the Broadband Universal Service Obligation
facts: The call invited prospective universal service providers to express interest.
The page explains that Ofcom was responsible for implementing the broadband USO.
limits: The consultation status is not a current designation decision.
Historic process evidence does not prove present eligibility.

sources.title: Broadband universal service goes live – advice for customers
sources.geo: United Kingdom eligible homes and businesses
facts: The scheme went live on 20 March 2020.
The page states the baseline of 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload for a decent connection.
limits: Thresholds and affordability figures are dated to the page's publication context.
Eligibility requires a current case-specific check.

sources.title: Compliance programme into access to emergency services
facts: The programme assessed uninterrupted emergency access and caller-location obligations.
Ofcom closed the programme without identifying issues requiring further formal enforcement at that time.
limits: Programme closure is not a universal compliance guarantee.
The record does not test a specific customer's emergency-call access.

sources.title: Compliance monitoring programme into access to emergency services during power outages
facts: The programme examined emergency access during customer-premises power outages.
Ofcom gathered information from more than 30 communications providers.
limits: The programme did not measure every network or premises.
Historic findings do not prove present resilience.

sources.title: Guidance: Protecting access to emergency organisations when there is a power cut at the customer’s premises
facts: The guidance addresses emergency calls over broadband during a premises power cut.
It sets out four principles for providers.
limits: The HTML summary is not the full guidance instrument.
Provider compliance depends on circumstances and implementation.

sources.title: Ofcom investigates BT and Three following mobile network outages
facts: Ofcom opened investigations into BT and Three after UK-wide voice disruptions.
The incidents included disruption to access to emergency services.
limits: An investigation announcement is not a finding of breach.
The incidents do not establish ongoing availability.
